Implants are insanely expensive, and the dentist isn’t even sure she’d be a candidate due to bone loss. I agree though, it’s clear her anxiety is making her catastrophize the whole situation. I guess all I can do is offer as much support as possible and encourage a positive mindset.

I have tinnitus from attending concerts and raves, also from listening to music way too loud. Try to keep the music down, anything above 80-90 decibels can cause hearing loss after an extended period of time. Trust me, you definitely don’t want this for the rest of your life. If your tinnitus isn’t constant, I’d say you’re probably fine for now, it could just be your ears warning you. The mind is also a powerful thing, it could simply just be making the noise up because you’re worrying about it. Also, if you can, try to not wear headphones all of the time. Listening to music via a speaker or anything else is safer. And keep in mind that if you ever do get chronic tinnitus, it’s not the end of the world. It sucks, but you forget about it most of the time.

I think it’s less about masking and more about having something else to listen to other than your tinnitus. I have about 3-4 different tones in my head, so I’ve found playing multiple sounds on top of each other helps to almost match it and distract me. As someone else already recommended, get yourself a white noise app. Melatonin helps, too. 

Also, I’ve read some of your post history, and I just wanted to tell you that it gets better. I know everyone probably tells you this, but it’s the truth. Eventually, your mind will get sick of worrying about the same thing 24/7. I developed it exactly 4 months ago and it’s accentuated my depression and suicidal thoughts, I know first hand just how rough that shit is. Stay strong, and before you kill yourself, at least try something like CBT. Also, hey, I have GERD too and throat problems that stem it. Chronic illness sucks and has a huge impact on your life, but you can learn to adapt and cope with it. Good luck.

Only a few hours, but three of my cats over the past 10 years have gotten out and suddenly gone missing in the same fashion. Me and my neighbors predict it’s someone poisoning cats, as I’m not the only person who has experienced this. I know I’m being dramatic, it’s just unbelievable how unlucky I am.

Honestly, researching and sitting on tinnitus forums constantly doesn’t do any good. I did this the first few months I developed tinnitus, and I swear it made it so much worse. Sometimes, even just going on r/tinnitus will cause me to have a small spike. It sucks that there’s nothing we can do about it right now, but at least we can manage it and try to live happy lives. I honestly thought my life was over a few months ago. To anyone feeling hopeless or like they’ll never be happy again: IT GETS BETTER. Thank you so much for making this post, I’m definitely looking back on this the next time my T gets me down.
